cross.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $χ$EFT and lattice QCD
cross.summary: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

cross.title: Exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in DHOST gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
cross.summary: Within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in General Relativity and DHOST gravity. Using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, Maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. This analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. Applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of DHOST class~Ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the DHOST constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. Based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between General Relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.

cross.title: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
cross.summary: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $\omega$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(\rho)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $\Theta = dI/d\omega = \widetilde{\Theta}/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tilde{\Theta}$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $\Theta$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation. The adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.

cross.title: Eccentricity detectability in Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals
cross.summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.

cross.title: Population inference of eccentric binary black holes using asymptotic constants of motion
cross.summary: In standard gravitational-wave population analyses of compact binaries, source parameters are defined at a reference frequency. For quantities that evolve during the inspiral, this means constructing a population of systems at different evolutionary stages, which complicates the astrophysical interpretation of the results. The past-time infinity, or zero-frequency, limit provides a mathematically well-defined reference where all sources enter the population fit on equal footing. This approach was first proposed for spin tilts, which evolve due to spin precession but converge to constant values as binaries are back-propagated. The orbital eccentricity also evolves throughout the inspiral and approaches unity in the zero-frequency limit for all binaries, making it unsuitable as a common reference point for population analyses. On the other hand, the Newtonian orbital angular momentum is an asymptotic constant of motion of the relativistic two-body problem and remains finite in this limit. In this paper, we make use of this known asymptotic behavior to reformulate eccentric population inference in terms of orbital angular momentum rather than eccentricity and demonstrate this approach on simulated gravitational-wave data. Our work constitutes the first example of eccentric population inference using only asymptotic constants of motion. Importantly, after the inference has been performed using this consistent reference, the results can be propagated to any preferred frequency for comparison with astrophysical predictions.

cross.title: Exploring a Correlation Between AGN Black Hole Mass and X-ray Luminosity
cross.summary: The traditional method to measure Type-1 Active Galactic Nuclei central black hole masses ($M_{BH}$) is the reverberation mapping (RM) technique. Motivated by the desire to find a less observationally expensive method (than RM) to estimate $M_{BH}$, we have explored a purported correlation between X-ray luminosity and $M_{BH}$. For this we have compiled a sample of 35 AGN with RM $M_{BH}$ estimates that were detected in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey public data release. Using a sample that is larger than that of J. A. Mayers et al. 2018 and has a cleaner selection function, we confirm their XMM-Newton based result of a positive correlation. However, the scatter on the scaling relation remains too high ($\sigma_\mathrm{int}=0.50^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$) to make this a practical method to predict $M_{BH}$ for a given X-ray detected Type-1 AGN. That said, our findings can be used to improve mock X-ray skies generated from large volume hydrodynamical cosmological simulations. Such mocks are a necessary ingredient for cluster cosmology and preparation for future missions such as NewAthena.

cross.title: Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures
cross.summary: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

cross.title: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
cross.summary: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

cross.title: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
cross.summary: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.

cross.title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
cross.summary: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

cross.title: Exceptional point excitation by a plunging particle
cross.summary: We investigate the excitation of a second-order exceptional point (EP) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum by a plunging particle. Starting from a gravitational action, we derive the master equation with a Gaussian bump modified potential. For the odd-parity mode $(\ell,m)=(2,1)$, we compute the waveform numerically and derive an analytic expression for the EP contribution to the ringdown waveform directly from the particle source. Comparison with the numerical waveform shows that the particle excites the EP response, which, together with its mirror contribution, dominates the intermediate ringdown stage. We use waveform fitting and Bayesian analysis to assess the limitations of conventional QNM templates for EP ringdown. In the fitting, the EP template recovers the complex frequency $\omega$ more accurately than the ordinary template. In Bayesian analysis, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $\rho=100$, the ordinary template yields a narrow frequency posterior whose $90\%$ credible region excludes the true EP frequency, whereas the broader EP-template region contains it. The Bayes factor nevertheless favors the ordinary template at lower SNRs and the EP template only at higher SNRs. These results show that in the EP case a narrow posterior and favorable Bayesian evidence do not guarantee accurate frequency inference when a conventional template omits the characteristic EP ringdown structure.

cross.title: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
cross.summary: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.

cross.title: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
cross.summary: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.

cross.title: Efficient Standard Siren Cosmological Inference with Posterior Reuse
cross.summary: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. Quantifying the effect of each choice typically requires a full, independent analysis. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. We apply the recently developed ASPIRE (Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference via Reuse) sampler to the joint estimation of cosmological and population parameters with dark sirens. ASPIRE updates existing posterior samples into the posterior under a new hypothesis without restarting from the prior. It combines normalising flows with a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to produce accurate posteriors and unbiased evidence estimates. Applying ASPIRE to a number of dark siren analysis cases with GWTC-5.0, we recover posteriors consistent with nested sampling, while recording a performance improvement of between 6-28 times over the set of analyses when using an existing posterior. This enables efficient exploration of modelling choices and rapid updates as catalogs grow, without duplicating existing computational effort.

cross.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
cross.summary: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted. We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained. We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0. Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

cross.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
cross.summary: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

cross.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
cross.summary: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

cross.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
cross.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $\nu_\tau$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

repl.title: Magnetars magnetic field evolution with ambipolar diffusion
repl.summary: The magnetic field associated with neutron stars is generally believed to be threaded inside the star. In the presence of a magnetic field, plasma in the interior of the star undergoes a series of processes that result in magnetic field evolution. It is believed that magnetar activities like X-ray, gamma-ray bursts, and giant flares (which release more energy in a few sec than Sun in 10 years), are mainly due to field decay. The most important process of field decay inside the core of the star is the ambipolar diffusion of the charged particles present in the interior plasma. The decay rate due to ambipolar diffusion is directly connected to the ambipolar velocity of the charged particles under the influence of the present magnetic field. The ambipolar velocity of the charged particles depends on the internal dynamics of the particles. We outline a general method to solve the particle dynamics in the presence of a magnetic field to have a magnetohydrodynamics equation from ambipolar velocity. The equation is general and applicable to all possible surrounding conditions temperature, matter states like normal or superfluid, etc.

repl.title: $^{56}$Ni production in long-lived binary neutron star merger remnants
repl.summary: We investigate the nucleosynthesis and kilonova emission based on numerical-relativity binary neutron star merger simulations that incorporate a two-moment neutrino-transport scheme. Unlike in previous works with simpler neutrino treatments, a massive, fast (up to $v=0.3c$), proton-rich neutrino-driven wind develops in the postmerger phase of the simulations as long as the merger remnant does not collapse to a black hole. We evolve the ejecta for 100 days after the merger using 2D ray-by-ray radiation-hydrodynamics simulations coupled in situ to a complete nuclear network. The most abundant nucleosynthesis products are He, $^{56}$Ni, and $^{56}$Co. We find a total yield of $\sim 10^{-3} M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni for all mergers that produce massive neutron star remnants, independently of the mass ratio and equations of state. After a few days, the decay of $^{56}$Ni and later $^{56}$Co becomes the primary source of heating in the matter expanding above the remnant. As a result, the kilonova light curve flattens on timescales of days for polar observation angles. This is an important effect that should be included in future models of kilonova light curves. Furthermore, the observation of a $^{56}$Ni-$^{56}$Co feature could serve as a clear indicator for the presence of a long-lived neutron star remnant in future kilonova observations.

repl.title: Flare genesis in relativistic jet: Disentangling the drivers of variability in the blazar 4C +27.50
repl.summary: Recently, blazar 4C +27.50 was found to be flaring in gamma-rays since its detection with Fermi-LAT in 2008. For the first time, a dedicated temporal and spectral study of the blazar 4C +27.50 has been performed in this work to understand the nature of this object. We used the Bayesian block algorithm to identify four flaring states and one quiet state in the 4-year-long Fermi-LAT light curve. Simultaneous broadband flaring episodes have been observed, and a significant correlation is seen between optical and $\gamma$-ray emission, suggesting the co-spatial origin of the broadband emission. The variation of fractional variability amplitude with respect to frequency shows a nearly double hump structure similar to broadband SED. The fastest flux doubling time in the 1-day binned $\gamma$-ray light curve is found to be about 7.8 hours. A curvature in $\gamma$-ray spectra has been observed, possibly caused by a stochastic particle acceleration process rather than radiative cooling. No evident correlation was found in the $\gamma$-ray flux-index plot, but a clear harder-when-brighter trend is observed in the X-ray flux-index plot. A one-zone leptonic model has been implemented to understand broadband emission during the quiet and flaring states, and the variation of the jet parameters has been investigated. Broadband SED modeling suggested that an enhancement in the magnetic field and particle energy density, together with a harder particle spectrum, might have caused the flaring events, while the bulk Lorentz factor shows no systematic change.

repl.title: Benchmarking the expected performance of Bayesian parameter inference on Kilonovae
repl.summary: In the study of optical transients, parameter inference is a part of the process of extracting physical information, i.e. constraints on the source's characteristics, by comparing the observed lightcurves to the predictions of different astrophysical models and finding the model and parameter combination that make the closest match. In the developing field of the study of kilonovae (KNe), systematic uncertainties in modeling are still very large. Current-day models still struggle to fit adequately the whole multi-wavelength dataset of the AT2017gfo kilonova, associated to the Binary Neutron Star (BNS) merger GW170817, and thus obtain wide posterior distributions on the inferred source parameters. After reviewing the many sources of uncertainty embedded in KN analyses and the process of Bayesian parameter inference, we discuss how to quantify the performance of parameter inference analyses using metrics on information gain from prior to posterior. We highlight the systematic error margin hyperparameter $\sigma_{\rm sys}$, which correlates to a model's goodness-of-fit, and exhibit its major influence on Bayesian inference performance metrics. Using the example of two KN models from the literature with the Nuclear Multi-Messenger Astronomy (NMMA) Bayesian inference framework, we simulate the expected information gains that dedicated KN follow-ups with telescope networks could reasonably reach, for various observational cadences and error margins: we show that the wind ejecta's mass and electron fraction are the easiest KN parameters to constrain. We finally apply our KN analysis to the dataset of AT2017gfo to show that our information gain predictions match results on real data and discuss the complementarity of multi-messenger approaches.

repl.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
repl.summary: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.

repl.title: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
repl.summary: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssim\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.

Unlike area-based summaries, it is not contaminated by the broad, potentially prior-sensitive direction associated with posterior elongation. Small values of λ ⟂ \lambda_{\perp} thus identify the region of strongest local reconstruction power. repl.title: Beyond Spin: QCD Magnetars
repl.summary: We present a unified framework in which anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs), soft gamma-ray repeaters (SGRs), superluminous supernovae (SLSNe-I), luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), and fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from quark deconfinement in the core of a massive neutron star (NS). Spontaneous ferromagnetism in the deconfined phase generates ~10^18 G core fields, producing a highly magnetized hybrid star (HS) -- the ``QCD magnetar'' -- whose surface field is set by NS mass, not birth spin. The Quark-Nova (QN) that forms the HS ejects ~ 0.01M_sun of neutron-rich outer layers, powering a kilonova and leaving the HS crustless for centuries. During this phase, magnetic instabilities at the hadron--quark interface release rising flux ropes that power X-ray-quiet FRBs; as the crust reforms, the source evolves into an X-ray-loud AXP&SGR. Two parameters govern the model: a critical mass M_dec triggering deconfinement, and a critical period P_fast separating fast and slow rotators. Fast rotators inject spin-down energy into the QN ejecta, producing an LFBOT -- directly observable once the SN ejecta is optically thin, or via binary accretion with no preceding SN; otherwise the LFBOT is reprocessed by the SN ejecta into an SLSN-I. A Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis reproduces the observed rates of AXPs\&SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~ 2.1M_sun and P_fast ~ 5.5 ms, and predicts non-merger r-process signatures and kilonovae from isolated NSs, with or without an LFBOT. The QN ejecta also carries its own DM and RM, independent of environment, predicted to appear as excess dispersion and rotation measure in FRBs in addition to the Galactic, host, and intergalactic contributions. These provide direct observational tests of the hadron--quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

repl.title: Comparison of the Neutron Star Birth Function from Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations with Observations
repl.summary: Using the mapping between progenitor core structure and the gravitational mass of neutron stars derived from sophisticated 3D supernova simulations, we construct the theoretical mass distribution of neutron stars at birth and investigate how it might comport with neutron star mass function measurements. In the process, we explore the effects of islands of black hole formation and subsequent mass accretion. We show that supernova theory can explain the observed neutron star mass function from its lower-mass peak near $\sim$1.35 $M_{\odot}$ to its higher-mass tail. Moreover, we suggest, but do not prove, that the lower predicted kick speeds expected during the birth of lower-mass neutron stars and the higher expected kick speeds expected on average for higher mass neutron stars may together sculpt the observed mass function in desired directions. The upshot of all these influences is to imprint upon the measured neutron star mass function features that reflect the varied physics of both neutron star origins and the neutron-star/black-hole dichotomy. Very approximately, we derive a black hole birth fraction of $\sim$19.6\%. In summary, we suggest that supernova theory can now be used to explain, however provisionally, various measured attributes of the population of compact objects and that an era of productive engagement between supernova theory and observation is at hand.

repl.title: Very High-Energy GRB Afterglow Fits with Neural-Network Emulation and Bayesian inference
repl.summary: The very high-energy ($E > 100$ GeV) afterglow emission in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) can be explained by synchrotron self-Compton (SSC). Modeling this emission accurately requires fully numerical codes that solve the time-dependent coupled particle--photon kinetic equations while accounting for Klein--Nishina suppression. However, their substantial computational cost makes them impractical for traditional parameter inference techniques such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. In this work, we present a highly efficient surrogate model based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) that emulates a one-zone kinetic SSC radiation code. To train our ANN, we use a multi-dimensional model parameter grid that constitutes a sample of 100,800 spectra produced by an infinitely thin spherical blast wave propagating inside a constant density interstellar medium (ISM). The ANN reproduces the numerical spectra well, with the median relative error generally below 2 per cent across the full frequency domain. Using this surrogate framework, we perform Bayesian parameter posterior estimation via MCMC and fit the broadband GRB afterglow observations of GRB 190114C from X-rays to TeV $\gamma$-rays at different epochs. We find an energetic jet with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k,iso}\simeq7.2\times10^{54}$ erg moving with a coasting bulk Lorentz factor of $\Gamma\gtrsim500$ into an ISM with density $n\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$. The deviation of our model light curve from observations on long timescales suggests that an ISM environment is inconsistent, and instead favours a radially stratified external medium.

repl.title: $r$-Process as Production of Lanthanides from Compact Object Mergers
repl.summary: The relative contributions of binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole-neutron star (BH-NS) mergers to the Galactic enrichment from the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remain an open question in nuclear astrophysics. In this paper, we present end-to-end numerical simulations of binary population synthesis, nucleosynthesis, and Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) via Compact Object Mergers: Population Astrophysics and Statistics (COMPAS), SkyNet network, and a stochastic multizone model, respectively. By considering five equations of state (EOSs) of NS and different spins of BH for BNS and BH-NS mergers, it is found that the averaged abundance seems not to be significantly dependent on the EOS of the neutron star (NS) and the spin of the BH for the BNS and BH-NS mergers. For the given EOSs of NS, the abundance of BNS is higher than that of BH-NS mergers before the second peak (for mass number $A\sim$130), but it is lower when the mass number is greater than 130. Moreover, the lighter $r$-process elements ($A<$130) are predominantly produced by the disk wind, while the heavier elements ($A>$130) originate mainly from the dynamical ejecta. The purely BNS mergers, on the other hand, are the dominant contributors to the production of lanthanides like europium (Eu) at the later stage of GCE, but BH-NS mergers make only a small contribution of heavy $r$-process elements for the $\rm Eu/Fe$ evolutionary tracks in the Milky Way.

repl.title: Wind-Fed Magnetic Flux and the Emergence of X-ray Coronae in Active Galactic Nuclei
repl.summary: We propose a scenario for the onset of radiatively efficient Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) in which circumnuclear stellar and supernova-driven winds supply mass and partially ordered magnetic flux to a compact disk reservoir around a supermassive black hole. A coherent poloidal component surviving advection to small radii strengthens inward, lowering the gas plasma beta until mean Maxwell stresses overtake MRI turbulence, compress the disk vertically, and open a magnetically dominated wedge above it. Within a quasi-force-free description of this wedge, the field self-organizes toward a critical twist at which the net radial transport changes sign, defining a magnetic saturation radius $r_c\sim10\,r_g$. The magnetic squeezing of the disk fixes the pressure balance at the interface between the disk and wedge, confining the accumulated flux at $r_c$: flux advected toward this boundary is preferentially shed, fixing $B_r\propto r^{-2}$ in the interior. From the field topology alone we then derive a normalized saturation flux $\phi \sim 50$, consistent with the MAD plateau of GRMHD simulations. The resulting compact, time-dependent saturation region is a natural candidate for the AGN X-ray corona, being collisionless, magnetized, and, at high compactness, plausibly pair-rich, with hadronic pair injection providing a conditional additional channel. Its size, variability, and spectral hardness are controlled by $r_c$, the compactness, and the magnetization. We connect these scalings to observed coronal sizes, variability, and the power partition between the corona and jet. We further propose that Little Red and Blue Dots could represent a disk-reservoir phase preceding luminous AGN activity.

repl.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
repl.summary: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.

repl.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
repl.summary: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

repl.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
repl.summary: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic variation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and hard X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. Furthermore, the flux variation is found to be anti-correlated with variation of the spectral photon index, that is, harder when brighter, in both gamma ray and hard X-ray bands. The origin of such variation is intriguing. Some possibilities are discussed.

repl.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
repl.summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.

repl.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
repl.summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_\nu \gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

repl.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
repl.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

repl.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
repl.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{a\gamma}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

repl.title: Astrophysics equation of state inference with Bayesian chiral effective field theory uncertainties
repl.summary: We investigate Bayesian chiral effective field theory ($\chi$EFT) uncertainties, which assign a statistical interpretation to equation of state (EOS) distributions near nuclear saturation density, n$_0$, as well as constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) to Bayesian EOS inference from LIGO/Virgo, NICER and pulsar mass observations. The tails of the $\chi$EFT uncertainties allow for broader pressure ranges in our priors, but large parts of these are excluded by the astrophysical observations, so that the EOS and the resulting mass-radius posteriors are still very consistent with our earlier work. Within our broad prior ranges, we observe a clear stiffening of the EOS at $n \gtrsim 3 n_0$. Moreover, the impact of the pQCD constraints on the posterior EOS and mass-radius range is negligible due to the astrophysics constraints. Exploiting the strong correlation between pure neutron matter and matter in beta equilibrium, we infer the symmetry energy slope parameter $L$ from astrophysics. For the $68\%$ credible interval, we obtain $L=42.6-52$ MeV and $L=44.2-56.7$ MeV using piecewise-polytrope and speed-of-sound high-density extensions, respectively. The $L$ posterior is mainly driven by the combination of GW170817 LIGO/Virgo and PSR J0740+6620, PSR J0437-4715, and PSR J0614-3329 NICER observations.

repl.title: Quasinormal modes and tidal responses of black holes in generic anisotropic matter environments
repl.summary: We develop a perturbative framework for a black hole embedded in a generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environment under spherical symmetry. Our approach extends previous analyses restricted to vanishing radial pressure or to perturbative matter configurations. Within this framework, we derive an analytical generalization of the Einstein cluster that incorporates a polytropic radial pressure, and we investigate the properties of this solution. We show that both the geodesic structure and the axial quasinormal-mode spectrum remain predominantly governed by an overall gravitational redshift effect, while the radial pressure systematically enhances the environmental corrections. In contrast, the tidal Love numbers are substantially more sensitive, and can exhibit order-unity deviations, including vanishing and negative strictly static magnetic Love numbers for sufficiently large anisotropy. We present the full linearized equations, which can be applied to various extensions, including ringdown analysis and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

repl.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
repl.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8\sigma$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5\sigma$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

repl.title: Horizon-scale intensity and polarization images of rotating Konoplya-Zhidenko black holes with thick accretion flows
repl.summary: We investigate the shadow and polarization images of a Konoplya--Zhidenko rotating non-Kerr black hole surrounded by a geometrically thick and optically thin accretion flow. The accretion flow is described by an analytical ballistic approximation accretion flow model. The numerical results show that the shadow image exhibits two main features, an outer bright ring and an inner dark region. The former corresponds to higher-order images, while the latter is associated with photon capture by the black hole. Increasing the deformation parameter $\eta$ does not significantly change the overall shape of the higher-order images, but it enlarges their size. Increasing either the spin parameter $a$ or the observer inclination angle $\theta_o$ enhances the asymmetry of the higher-order images and makes the intensity on the left side much larger than that on the right side. This behavior is associated with frame dragging and the relativistic Doppler effect. In the polarization images, the degree of linear polarization is much smaller in the higher-order image region than in other regions, and the polarization vectors extend over the whole image plane. Within the framework used in this work, these results illustrate how the spacetime geometry and near-horizon accretion dynamics jointly influence the intensity and polarization images.

repl.title: On the Nucleon Effective Mass in Neutron Stars Cooling
repl.summary: The cooling of neutrons stars, which are composed of ultra-high-density nuclear matter, strongly depends on the equation of state because the dominant cooling sources are neutrinos produced in their interiors. Here, we investigate the cooling properties of neutron stars, focusing on effective nucleon masses, whose impacts have been recently examined in supernova explosion and proto-neutron star cooling. The uncertainties of effective masses originate from the difference in the attractive interaction of scalar meson and the definition of the Dirac and Landau masses. At first, we employ so-called Walecka models that allow these two masses to be introduced within a unified framework and evaluate the resulting cooling curves. Based on the Walecka model, we compute the emissivity of the neutrons and the direct Urca process and their cooling curves. We demonstrate that the Dirac and Landau masses affect cooling of massive neutron stars, although most previous cooling simulations do not distinguish them. We also perform cooling simulations with two realistic equation of states based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory, whose differences arise from properties of only effective masses among characteristic parameters. These results are broadly consistent with those obtained from the Walecka models, indicating that the treatment of effective nucleon masses may be an important source of uncertainty in neutron-star cooling.

repl.title: Two-Fluid Schwarzschild Solution
repl.summary: \We consider the interior two-fluid Schwarzschild solution. That is a model of compact (neutron) stars with admixed dark matter. The two constant energy densities generalize the interior Schwarschild solution to the case of two fluids (representing standard model matter and dark matter, for instance), interacting mutually solely by the common gravitational field. In general, the two-fluid core is surrounded by a one-fluid corona (envelope). Only for special parameters (the model depends on energy densities $e_1,e_2$ and central pressures $p_{\mathrm{c}1},p_{\mathrm{c}2}$ of the fluids), both fluids occupy the same region. Despite the sum of two energy densities in that region, the compactness bound of 4/9 is not exceeded. Therefore, a Buchdahl limit for two fluids holds. A conceivable object is one with a stark leakage of one fluid (e.g. dark matter) beyond the two-fluid core.

repl.title: AI-Assisted Extraction of Follow-up Observations from GCN Circulars in Astro-COLIBRI
repl.summary: We present a new Astro-COLIBRI component that converts free-text GCN Circulars into structured, event-linked follow-up records and combines them with reports submitted directly by the community. A continuously running listener associates new Circulars with transient events, applies deterministic pre-analysis, and invokes a schema-constrained large language model to extract photometry, contacts, redshifts, and related metadata. The records are normalized into a common event-level database and exposed through the web and mobile interfaces as report summaries, contact tools, optical-afterglow context figures, and downloadable CSV or VOTable products. All 1,775 Circulars of an operational evaluation corpus covering the first half of 2026 completed the workflow without failures. An internal human audit of 210 Circulars found 223 of 231 assessed reports (96.5%) fully confirmed, each of the eight remaining ones containing at least one incorrect field, predominantly associated with observation timing and facility attribution. Extracted redshifts agree with three published compilations for 91.7 to 99.3% of the events they share, every disagreement tracing to a limit, a candidate-host estimate, or a later-refined value rather than to a misread Circular. The extraction also recovers 90 to 97% of the redshifts those compilations list for bursts it processed. Applied to the GCN archive since 2016, the pipeline yields 68,393 observations from 26,811 reports across 5,787 transient events, and now runs in real time on new Circulars. The reusable parsing and normalization pipeline is released as the open-source Python package astro-colibri-circular-parser.

repl.title: Sub-MeV gamma-ray lines from an endothermic interpretation of the LZ recoil candidate
repl.summary: Endothermic upscattering of heavy dark matter offers a compelling interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil candidate recently reported by LUX-ZEPLIN, with a characteristic recoil energy $E_R \propto \delta$, where $\delta$ is the mass splitting between the dark matter states. Cosmological and experimental constraints motivate the depletion of the primordial heavier state, which can be regenerated in the Galactic halo. We show that, if the heavier state decays radiatively, the same mass splitting sets the energy of a gamma-ray line, $E_\gamma \simeq \delta$. For our benchmark, this leads to a sub-MeV line within the projected reach of the Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), scheduled for launch in 2027. The confirmation of the LUX-ZEPLIN candidate event as a dark matter signal would therefore motivate dedicated searches for sub-MeV gamma-ray lines, with COSI providing a timely opportunity to test this interpretation.

repl.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
repl.summary: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

repl.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
repl.summary: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.
